associations.evidence_summary: The original historic chapel is part of the Meritxell Marian pilgrimage complex and remains separately identified from the newer basilica.
associations.qualification: Not an additional independently mapped pin until the two physical chapel identities and entrance are reconciled.

associations.evidence_summary: The ancient venerated image of Our Lady of Meritxell was destroyed in the fire of September 1972; a modern replacement is venerated.
associations.qualification: A lost image is not a presently conserved relic, and images in old and new church should not be conflated.

associations.evidence_summary: Belarusian Redemptorists record a Catholic pilgrimage visiting the sanctuary of the Queen of the Lakes in Braslaw.
associations.qualification: A historical pilgrimage itinerary does not establish exact present services, path geometry, or shrine juridical status.

associations.evidence_summary: Catholic Redemptorist pilgrims visited the Marian sanctuary at Gudogaj, separately from the sanctuary at Braslaw.
associations.qualification: The source attests a pilgrimage visit, but no current source-valid opening timetable or GPS entrance.

associations.evidence_summary: The Catholic Redemptorist pilgrimage record refers to the Mosar Hill of Crosses during its devotional journey.
associations.qualification: The hill's exact boundaries and its relation to the nearby parish church remain unresolved.

associations.evidence_summary: Bosnian Catholic heritage lists the historic Marian Catholic Assumption shrine at Olovo as a devotional destination.
associations.qualification: Historical Marian church tradition does not itself establish an approved apparition or relic authenticity.

associations.evidence_summary: Catholic Church and regional reporting document the Assumption pilgrimages to Kondžilo hill, distinct from the Olovo sanctuary.
associations.qualification: The hillside sanctuary and Komušina parish's associated icon are not automatically the same physical Place.

associations.evidence_summary: Local Bosnian Catholic sources describe annual Marian Assumption observances involving the hill of Kondžilo.
associations.qualification: A Bosnian local pilgrimage custom is not generalized as an established French domestic practice.

associations.evidence_summary: Saint Dominic's Catholic Church in Pasiene welcomes pilgrims and maintains Catholic Marian prayer and devotion.
associations.qualification: An active Catholic parish with pilgrims is not thereby established as a designated national sanctuary.

associations.evidence_summary: Pasiene's parish presents devotional observances and Marian prayer associated with its own pilgrim ministry.
associations.qualification: Local Latvian Catholic custom remains a regional record, not an automatic French Catholic usage.

associations.evidence_summary: Luxembourg archdiocesan accounts distinguish the historic Marian Glacis chapel from Notre-Dame Cathedral during the Octave.
associations.qualification: The Marian image now kept at the cathedral must not be assigned to the historic Glacis chapel.

associations.evidence_summary: Catholic Luxembourg sources document a Marian Octave prayer tradition associated with the Glacis chapel and cathedral.
associations.qualification: This is a local Luxembourg devotional history with francophone borderland relevance, not a rule of French domestic practice.

associations.evidence_summary: Monaco's Catholic cathedral is a distinct principal church in the principality's religious heritage itinerary.
associations.qualification: The cathedral's princely tombs are secular burials, not saintly relic collections.

associations.evidence_summary: Monaco's official churches itinerary independently identifies the Catholic Church of Saint Charles.
associations.qualification: Inclusion on a tourism itinerary does not make the church an episcopally designated pilgrimage sanctuary.

associations.evidence_summary: Heritage descriptions link Kotor's Catholic cathedral with the traditional relics of its patron Saint Tryphon.
associations.qualification: Secondary destination reporting is insufficient to certify exact current custodial inventory or relic authenticity.

associations.evidence_summary: The historic Roman Catholic Cathedral of Saint Tryphon remains a named patronal heritage destination in Kotor.
associations.qualification: Cathedral identity alone must not be misrepresented as a current official annual pilgrim programme.

associations.evidence_summary: The Gibraltar diocese identifies the cathedral and its devotional Lourdes chapel as part of a single church complex.
associations.qualification: Lourdes chapel inside cathedral must not generate a second building or imply Marian apparitions took place in Gibraltar.

associations.evidence_summary: Vaduz's current Catholic Saint Florin cathedral remains distinguishable from the earlier chapel superseded in the nineteenth century.
associations.qualification: The dedication and cathedral's pilgrimage/heritage context do not independently prove formal national shrine status.

associations.evidence_summary: Catholic authorities and Aid to the Church in Need document Saint Mother Teresa's Cathedral in Pristina and its 2017 consecration.
associations.qualification: Patron saint dedication is not proof of physical custody of Mother Teresa relics or a miraculous apparition.

governance: At Meritxell, old chapel and new basilica are distinct buildings; 1972 fire destroyed the old venerated image, modern statue is a reproduction.
At Luxembourg, the Glacis chapel is physically distinct from Cathedral Notre-Dame, although original votive image migrated to the cathedral.
Kondžilo hill sanctuary and Olovo shrine are different sites; Marian pilgrimage does not prove approved apparitions or independent miracles.
Mosar pilgrimage hill is not automatically a canonical standalone church; site and precise identity still need review.
Pasiene's parish website confirms active Marian practice but does not designate a national shrine.
Monaco royal tombs are not relics of canonized saints.
Gibraltar cathedral's Lourdes chapel belongs INSIDE the cathedral; do not add a second building pin for an embedded chapel.
Kotor saint relic attribution rests on historical destination reporting until an original custodian inventory is verified.
All source site candidates held from production: no GPS, generated routes, schedules, biographies, or reuse of images.
